The new security challenges of the 21stcentury are of a different nature since they are not necessarily generated by countries with conventional weapons or geographically limited in certain areas. Globalization is increasing the range, scale and capabilities of the threats and also the likelihood of conflict involving non-state and failed-state actors. Asymmetric tactics such as economic, cyber and proxy actions instead of direct military confrontation will play an increasing part; therefore we must have the capacity to anticipate and protect against changing security challenges, from terrorism, cyberattacks, and the proliferation of CBRN weapons. intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly central to cybersecurity operations in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments, ensuring ethical alignment and human oversight has never been more critical. This chapter explores the integration of ethical AI principles and human-in-the-loop (HILT) frameworks within cybersecurity architectures deployed across hybrid cloud infrastructures. It addresses the unique risks posed by autonomous decision-making in high-stakes industrial contexts\u2014such as manufacturing, energy, and logistics\u2014where errors can lead to cascading operational and safety consequences. The chapter gives a multi-disciplinary background by overviewing some of the fundamental concepts of AI ethics and current use of AI in IIoT related to cybersecurity, as well as the role of human control in reducing opacity, bias and mistakes in algorithms. It displays how HITL models can be successfully integrated to advance threat detection, human operator-AI collaboration and system accountability using real-world case
